answer:
The design treats growth marketing as a closed optimization loop: an operator sets a **constrained objective**, the system proposes copy, targeting, and event-definition changes, executes only approved ones on ad platforms, measures results, and feeds evidence back into a reviewed release process.

The automated-writing scope is well-matched to established practice: AI writing is already common in sales, marketing, and team communication, including ad copywriting and product descriptions (Chapter 1, p.40), and AI can make user acquisition cheaper through more effective copywriting and promotional content (Chapter 1, p.52).

**Engineering inference:** the hard part is not generation but the write path — external ad mutations cost money and are only partially reversible, so the architecture is organized around an approval boundary and an idempotent execution layer rather than around the model.

**Step 1–3 (decide).** The Growth Operator Console defines objective, budgets, brand guardrails, and approval policy in the Objective & Constraint Service. Each cycle, the Campaign Optimization Orchestrator loads that scope plus the released optimization config from the Prompt & Model Registry, then validates every candidate action against constraints and receives a pass/violation verdict.

**Step 4 (compose).** Three specialists produce proposals, never external writes:
- *Copy Generation Service* fetches approved prompt/template versions from the registry, validates brand rules, and persists versioned drafts to the Creative Artifact Store.
- *Targeting & Audience Service* reuses audience definitions with staleness and provenance checks, persisting revalidated versions, using released targeting heuristics.
- *Event Definition Service* versions conversion-event specs and checks schema compatibility against the Outcome Event Stream contract before anything can sync to a platform.

**Execution.** Only after approval does the Channel Execution Service call Ad & Analytics Platforms with a reserved idempotency key, handling COMMITTED / NOT_FOUND-retry / STILL_UNKNOWN-escalation, plus authoritative read-back for intended-vs-actual reconciliation.

**Step 5–6 (measure).** Platform conversion and spend events — delayed, duplicated, out of order — enter Outcome Ingestion with bounded backpressure and dedup, flow through the durable replayable stream, and are attributed and written with lineage to the Outcome & Spend Store. Measurement & Attribution scores variants against the objective and returns performance plus constraint adherence to the orchestrator.

The Approval Boundary Service is the single gate between proposing and spending. It classifies each typed **exact-action** proposal by risk and cost, then:
- **auto-approves** in-policy low-risk changes (e.g., copy swaps within brand guardrails);
- **routes** costly or irreversible actions — budget increases, new event definitions, audience expansion beyond thresholds — to the console as pending proposals with full context, awaiting an explicit operator decision;
- **blocks** execution until decided, so no path reaches the platforms without a recorded verdict.

Crucially, compensation and rollback actions after a partial failure re-enter the *same* gate (n9 → n8 → n9), so error recovery cannot bypass policy.

A second, separate boundary governs learning: release candidates go from Offline Evaluation to the Release Manager, which presents them to the operator for human release review before any registry write. Live optimization behavior changes only through that reviewed release path, not through online self-mutation.

Measured outcomes and constraint violations flow to the Feedback Curation Service, which builds versioned evaluation datasets (including hostile traces) — the rule being no model or config change without curated evidence. Offline Evaluation runs regression gates against acceptance thresholds; the Release Manager performs canary rollout, metric-gated promotion using live canary metrics from Measurement, and immediate rollback on regression. The Prompt & Model Registry is storage only; mutation occurs solely via the Release Manager.

Observability & Audit records proposal provenance, approval decisions, execution/reconciliation events, and release outcomes, and runs drift and anomaly detection, alerting the operator.

**Note on writes:** although no *business* mutation reaches ad platforms without approval, the system continuously writes internally — artifact versions, outcome records, audit logs, curated datasets, and registry releases are all state changes with their own lifecycle and rollback needs.

**Engineering inference:** attribution quality is the weak link in the eval loop; scored results are only as trustworthy as the event definitions and attribution window, so event-definition changes should be treated as evaluation-invalidating and force a dataset version bump.

- **Approval granularity vs. optimization speed.** A tight auto-approve envelope makes spend safe but slows the loop to human cadence; a wide one lets the orchestrator explore faster at real financial risk. Recommendation: start with copy-only auto-approval and expand thresholds using audited outcome history.
- **Measurement latency vs. iteration rate.** Conversions arrive late and out of order; scoring too early rewards noise. Recommendation: hold decisions until a configured attribution maturity window, and use the stream's replay capability to re-score rather than re-decide.
- **Reviewed releases vs. online adaptation.** Gating prompts, heuristics, and config behind canary and human review reduces regression blast radius but means the system cannot adapt mid-cycle to sudden market shifts; consider a narrowly-scoped, constraint-bounded bid-adjustment exception.
- **External dependency.** Platform APIs are third-party and may return ambiguous mutation results; the reserve-then-read-back design contains this but leaves a STILL_UNKNOWN escalation class that needs a defined operator runbook.

**Uncertainty:** the value of automated event-definition changes depends heavily on the specific platforms' tracking semantics, which the design assumes rather than establishes.

The diagram described above was created and rendered on the canvas as this turn's approved graph.

graph.title: AI Growth & Performance Marketing Optimization System

nodes.label: Growth Operator Console
nodes.description: Primary actor UI: defines objective, constraints, budgets, and approval policy; reviews pending proposals; confirms or rejects costly mutations before any external write.

nodes.label: Objective & Constraint Service
nodes.description: Owns the constrained objective, budget caps, brand and policy guardrails; validates every proposed action against constraints before it may proceed to approval or execution.

nodes.label: Campaign Optimization Orchestrator
nodes.description: Runs optimization cycles: reads measured outcomes, decides copy, targeting, and event-definition changes to maximize the objective within constraints; issues proposals, never direct external writes.

nodes.label: Copy Generation Service
nodes.description: Writes and adjusts ad copy variants using approved prompts and templates; validates brand-rule compliance; persists versioned drafts to the artifact store before proposing them.

nodes.label: Targeting & Audience Service
nodes.description: Proposes and adjusts audience segments, bids, and placement targeting; reuses validated audience definitions from the artifact store with invalidation on staleness.

nodes.label: Event Definition Service
nodes.description: Owns conversion event definitions and tracking specs; versions changes, enforces schema compatibility with the outcome stream, and flags definitions needing approval before platform sync.

nodes.label: Creative Artifact Store
nodes.description: Versioned store for copy, targeting, and event artifacts; owns retrieval validation, reuse lifecycle, and invalidation so only current approved artifacts are proposed or executed.

nodes.label: Approval Boundary Service
nodes.description: Enforces approval boundaries: classifies each proposal by risk and cost, routes human-confirmation items to the console with full context, auto-approves only in-policy low-risk changes, and blocks execution until decided

nodes.label: Channel Execution Service
nodes.description: Executes approved changes to ad platforms: reserve-before-send with atomic idempotency keys, retry-safe writes, reconciliation of intended vs actual platform state, and compensation or rollback on partial failure.

nodes.label: Ad & Analytics Platforms
nodes.description: External ad networks and analytics APIs that serve campaigns, accept mutation calls, and expose outcome and spend data; owned by third parties outside this system.

nodes.label: Outcome Ingestion Service
nodes.description: Ingests conversion and spend events from platforms and trackers; owns bounded backpressure, event-time ordering rules, replay and deduplication, late-data handling, and schema compatibility checks.

nodes.label: Outcome Event Stream
nodes.description: Durable ordered buffer decoupling ingestion from measurement; supports replay for reprocessing and consumer isolation during failures.

nodes.label: Outcome & Spend Store
nodes.description: Canonical deduplicated record of conversions, spend, and delivery metrics with lineage to source events; golden source for measurement, evaluation, and budget reconciliation.

nodes.label: Measurement & Attribution Service
nodes.description: Evaluates outcomes against the objective: attributes conversions to variants, computes performance and constraint adherence, and publishes scored results back to the orchestrator and evaluation.

nodes.label: Feedback Curation Service
nodes.description: Curates labeled evidence from measured outcomes (winning/losing variants, constraint violations) into versioned evaluation datasets; no model or config change without curated evidence.

nodes.label: Offline Evaluation Service
nodes.description: Runs offline evaluation and regression gates for prompt, model, and targeting-heuristic candidates against curated datasets and acceptance thresholds before any release review.

nodes.label: Release Manager Service
nodes.description: Executes reviewed releases of models, prompts, rankings, and live optimization config: human release review, canary rollout, metric-gated promotion, and immediate rollback on regression.

nodes.label: Prompt & Model Registry
nodes.description: Versioned registry of prompts, models, and optimization configs with evaluation history and release status; storage only, mutation occurs solely via the Release Manager.

nodes.label: Observability & Audit Service
nodes.description: End-to-end audit of proposals, approvals, executions, and releases; drift and anomaly detection on outcomes and model behavior; defined failure isolation and alerting for operator review.

assumptions: Ad and analytics platforms expose APIs for campaign writes and outcome retrieval; the system is authorized to mutate campaigns on connected accounts.
The operator sets the objective (e.g., maximize conversions), constraints (budget caps, brand rules), and approval policy; the system optimizes within them.

Costly or irreversible mutations (budget increases, new event definitions, audience expansion beyond thresholds) require explicit human approval; low-risk copy swaps within guardrails may auto-approve.
Outcome data arrives as a continuous event stream with possible delays, duplicates, and out-of-order delivery.
Learning loop updates prompts, copy templates, targeting heuristics, and live optimization configuration through a reviewed release process, not direct online mutation.
Third-party ad platforms, attribution data sources, and end-user tracking are external systems outside this boundary.
